query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a ductile, rare-earth-free metallic phase can enhance the integrity of the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy without sacrificing its caloric response.
generation.intervention: Incorporation of a ductile metallic phase (e.g., Cu, Ag) via mechanical alloying or spark plasma sintering
generation.conditions: Applied magnetic field: 0-5 Tesla, pressure: 0-100 MPa, temperature: 250-350 K, loading regime: uniaxial compression
generation.structural_mediator: Ductile phase distribution and its interaction with the high-entropy alloy matrix
generation.mechanism: The ductile phase acts as a crack-arresting medium, enhancing the alloy's toughness and integrity while maintaining its caloric response due to the preservation of the high-entropy alloy's microstructure
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved compressive strength (> 200 MPa) and toughness (> 10% increase in strain to failure) without a significant decrease in caloric response (< 10% reduction in entropy change)
generation.boundary: Maximum operating temperature: 400 K, maximum applied pressure: 200 MPa
generation.uncertainty: The optimal ductile phase content and distribution for maximizing the alloy's integrity and caloric response are unknown

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled comparison of the caloric response and mechanical properties of the modified alloy with the baseline alloy under identical conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the modified alloy exhibits a > 20% decrease in caloric response or a < 10% increase in compressive strength compared to the baseline alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
